reader.requirement: At 85 an input-output statement on a relative file that succeeds (OPEN, CLOSE, READ, WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE, START in every access mode) sets an I-O status of the successful class 0x (00, 04, 05), and no USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure runs for it.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility (from 2002): off at 85, so no 5x/6x sharing status can replace a 1985 value; a second OPEN of an open physical file through another file-name is not a sharing conflict

reader.notes: Every successful arm sets a 0x status, and the generated __IoCheck returns before any declarative tier when status[0] is '0' (IoStatusClass.Successful), at every edition. The status class tests (CodeGen/Verbs/IoStatusClass.cs), the generated __IoCheck hook (DispatchEmitter.EmitUseMachinery) and the Status setter's permanent-error record are the same code at every edition. A relative READ answers 04 only on a file whose OPEN could not check its record bounds (docs/conformance/3/D-IO-STATUS-04, a zero-byte store); a sequential reader opened on such a store does not see later records, so 04 was witnessed on the random path only.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VIII.1.3.4 whole (the relative list has no 02/07: no relative CLOSE or OPEN format carries NO REWIND/REEL/REMOVAL). runs/rc1-001..rc4-001 at --std 85: CLOSE relative WITH NO REWIND -> COBOL1693, CLOSE REEL -> COBOL1693, OPEN INPUT WITH NO REWIND -> COBOL1802, CLOSE FOR REMOVAL -> COBOL2269, so 07 is unreachable as the relative list requires. runs/r1a-001: OPEN INPUT of an absent OPTIONAL relative file with USE ON INPUT -> 'OI 05 USES 00' (no USE for a successful completion; file not created), OPEN I-O of an absent OPTIONAL dynamic file -> 'OD 05 USES 01' unchanged (file created, later WRITE 00 / READ 00 DDDD). Edition sites: RelativeConnector.Write's DialectBehavior arm and FileConnector.SharingFacilityInEffect are the only IO-runtime edition reads on the path (grep DialectBehavior/Edition in RelativeConnector, KeyedConnector, FileConnector, FileRegistry). cite.py: 'OK §1985:VIII.1.3.4 GRL2.1 (1.3.4 I-O Status) the text is in GRL2.1'.
